<Route path="/ade/dashboard/versions" />

An OpenAPI document can use definitions that live at another address, such as
`{"$ref": "https://schemas.acme.com/common.json#/Money"}`. The **References** tab on **Versions**
shows what a revision depends on from outside, when each one was last fetched, and whether it has
changed since. It also lists the document's **circular references**, the internal `$ref`s that
lead back to themselves.

<Screenshot id="project-references" alt="The References tab: the external reference policy, three external references (one Changed with its changes open, one Up to date, one Blocked because its host is not allowlisted) and one circular reference" />

## Open the tab

1. Open **Versions** and pick the project.
2. **Click the “References” tab**, then pick the **Revision**.

The tab reads the revision's OpenAPI document as it was imported. A revision imported from several
files has no single document to read. Export it as one bundled file and import that file instead.

## The references

There is one row per URL. A URL used in several places (`common.json#/Money`,
`common.json#/Tax`) is one row, and **Used at** lists every place.

| Column | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| **Reference** | The URL, without its `#` fragment. |
| **Used at** | How many `$ref`s use it. Open it to see each JSON Pointer. |
| **Status** | What the last refresh found (see below). |
| **Last fetched** | When the document was last fetched, and the start of its sha-256 digest. |
| **Pinned** | The digest of the pinned document, if the reference is pinned. |

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Not fetched** | No one has refreshed this reference yet. |
| **Up to date** | The document has not changed: it matches its pin, or the previous fetch if it is not pinned. |
| **Changed** | The document is different. **Show changes** lists what changed. |
| **Unreachable** | The host did not answer, answered with an error, or did not send JSON or YAML. The last fetched document is kept. |
| **Blocked** | The fetch was not allowed. The row says why: the policy, the allowlist, a private address, or fetching turned off for the deployment. |

## Refresh

**Click “Refresh all”**, or the refresh button on one row. Apiome fetches each document now. It
does not reuse an earlier download, so a change on the remote host is always seen. It then
compares the new document with:

- the **pinned** document, if the reference is pinned;
- otherwise, the **previous fetch**. The first fetch of a reference has nothing to compare with,
  so it reads **Up to date**.

A changed reference reads **Changed**. **Click “Show changes”** to see each changed value: its JSON
Pointer, whether it was **Added**, **Removed** or **Changed**, and the value before and after. The
list shows up to 200 changes and counts the rest.

Refreshing needs permission to edit the project. Each refresh, and each change it finds, is
recorded in the audit log (`project.external_refs.refreshed`, `project.external_ref.changed`).

## Pin

**Click the pin** on a row to accept the document it last fetched. While a reference is pinned,
every refresh compares against the pin. A remote change therefore stays **Changed** until you
review it and pin again. An unpinned reference compares with the previous fetch, so a change shows
only once.

**Click the crossed-out pin** to unpin. A reference must have been fetched before it can be pinned.

## Circular references

**Circular references** lists each loop of internal references, for example
`#/components/schemas/Category → #/components/schemas/Node → #/components/schemas/Category`. A
self-recursive schema is a loop of one. Loops are valid OpenAPI. When you
[export a spec dereferenced](/ship/export-a-spec), the reference that closes each loop is kept as a
`$ref` rather than expanded forever.

## The external reference policy

The policy at the top of the tab decides which URLs Apiome may fetch. It applies to every project
in the workspace, and to [repository scans](../bring-in/repositories.mdx#references-to-schemas-outside-the-repository).

| Mode | What is fetched |
| --- | --- |
| **Block** (the default) | Nothing. Every reference reads **Blocked** when refreshed. |
| **Fetch** | Any public host. If the allowlist is not empty, only the hosts on it. |
| **Fetch allowlisted hosts only** | Only hosts on the allowlist, which must not be empty. |

Workspace administrators **click “Change policy”**, choose the **Mode**, list the
**Allowed hosts** one per line, and **click “Save policy”**. A host is written as
`schemas.acme.com`, `*.acme.com` (any subdomain, not `acme.com` itself) or `*` (any host). Each
change is recorded in the access audit log (`governance.external_ref_policy.update`).

Whatever the policy says, Apiome never fetches a private or local address, and follows only
`http` and `https`. A deployment can also turn fetching off entirely
(`remote_ref_resolution_allowed`). The policy line then says so, and every reference reads
**Blocked**.

## REST API

| Call | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/projects/{tenant_slug}/{project_id}/references?version=…` | The references, their status and pins, the cycles and the policy. |
| `POST …/references/refresh` | Fetch every reference now, or only the `urls` given. |
| `PUT …/references/pin` · `DELETE …/references/pin?url=…` | Pin or unpin a reference. |
| `GET` · `PUT /v1/tenants/{tenant_slug}/governance/external-ref-policy` | Read the policy (any member), or change it (administrators). |

See the [project references reference](/reference/rest/project-references). Refusals carry a
`code`: `ref-not-fetched` (409, pin before any fetch), `ref-not-found` (404), `unknown-reference`
(422, a URL the revision does not use), `invalid-allowlist` and `allowlist-required` (422).
